question: Should OpenClaw send user-requested HealthKit aggregates to any configured AI provider under this consent model, treating that provider interaction as the permitted health or fitness service?
rationale: Apple permits third-party HealthKit disclosure only with prior express consent and for the third party to provide the corresponding health or fitness service; code review cannot choose the permanent product, provider, and compliance boundary.

options.title: Approve bounded provider disclosure
options.body: Accept the fixed aggregate schema for configured providers after foreground handling, provider-use constraints, release privacy updates, and signed-device proof are complete.

options.title: Restrict eligible providers
options.body: Permit the feature only for local models or providers whose data-use terms satisfy the HealthKit service and no-data-mining boundary.

options.title: Keep Health data on device
options.body: Reject provider disclosure and limit HealthKit support to local presentation or on-device processing.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded provider disclosure
recommendation.body: Accept the fixed aggregate schema for configured providers after foreground handling, provider-use constraints, release privacy updates, and signed-device proof are complete.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior merged iOS permission, capability-routing, and Swift-policy work makes this the strongest history-based owner for the product boundary, with release review from joshavant.
